The best free to play game on the market

[h1] Free to Play Worth Paying For [/h1]

Overview: One of the best and most addicting Free-to-Play games I’ve ever played. Warframe boasts a polished movement system, strong visuals, loads of unlocks, and some of the strongest third-person action gameplay on the market.

Pros: 
+ Incredibly polished combat and movement systems
+ A plethora of unlockable warframes, weapons, items, and cosmetics
+ One of the friendliest online communities on Steam
+ Appealing visuals
+ A generous and fair microtransaction system

Cons: 
-	Storytelling falls flat and quests are boring to complete
-	Alternate game modes such as the arcwing are just not fun
-	Some free-to-play elements become especially grating (especially the timers)

****    ****    ****

Free-to-Play games are hard to review. A big part of that is the price which looms over you. When I try to analyze or critique a certain aspect, I’m reminded that at the end of the day, it’s free. I didn’t pay a dime to download the game and start it. In the end, the only thing I’m investing here is my time. This goes double for Warframe; a free-to-play game that is not only polished but has some of the most sensible and fair monetization schemes in the industry. What follows is my attempt to reconcile the game’s business practices with the actual experience of the game. I seek to answer the question, is the game worth your time? 

Well the answer is, yes. It definitely is. I could harp on Warframe’s strengths for a while. The combat system here is incredible. Everything is so fast and fluid. Weapon switching, shooting, and movement is seamless, flowing from one action to another without any sort of pause. One moment you’re mowing down hordes of mooks with your automatic rifle, the next you’re flying through the air in bullet-time dual wielding pistols, then landing with a crash to slice a guy with a greatsword. Make no mistake, Warframe is a power fantasy through-and-through, and every quest, story, and moment of gameplay seeks to reinforce that feeling. Combat is made better with the incredible parkour, offering unparalleled movement and traversal, including wallrunning, gliding, dashing, and sliding. The more skilled players can dash through levels in seconds, barely touching the ground as they go yet still destroying every enemy in sight. 

The titular warframes are the highlight, with dozens available to you, each with a different theme and superpowers. There are DPS, tank, and support warframes, for example. It’s almost guaranteed you’ll find something that fits your style. Weapons are remarkably varied. You’ll have a primary weapon like a rifle or shotgun, a secondary weapon like a revolver or kunai, and a melee weapon like a greatsword or my favorite knuckle dusters. In another game, the developer would be content to offer a limited selection of weapon types, simply tweaking the numbers to artificially inflate how many weapons there are. Not so here; each weapon feels interesting, unique, and different. You’ll spend a significant amount of time here grinding as you aim to unlock that new gun or warframe. 

Speaking of which, warframe has some insane grinding. You’d better be ready for it. This is one of the most grindy games I’ve ever come across and you may spend dozens of hours just to unlock that one warframe or item you want, unless you plan on spending money. Being a free-to-play game, I could hardly begrudge it that – it certainly earns it. That said, some of the free-to-play mechanics did wear on me considerably. The timers were especially egregious. To build pretty much any item in the game, you need to wait for the timer to run out. So, you want to build a specific weapon? Well not only must you have the proper mastery rank AND blueprint to create it. You must obtain all the materials for it and wait 12 hours before you can use that weapon you want. It’s even worse for warframes. Where you must obtain three separate blueprints for each component, each with a 12-hour timer THEN wait THREE WHOLE DAYS to assemble all the warframe components. 

With that said, I find very hard to even hold it against the game. Its free-to-play, the platinum prices (in-game currency) are reasonably priced, PLUS the game allows you to gain platinum by trading with other players. So, I feel it levels out, somewhat, even if I despise the timers. 

The only criticism I can confidently level at warframe is the story and quest design. This is the weakest aspect of warframe by far. I often found quests to be tedious and boring with uninteresting objectives, incoherent storytelling coupled with mediocre voice acting. Often quests are the exact same things you would do in a regular mission except now it has a story behind it, as we’re led to believe. 

I especially hated the reveal at the middle part of the game, where its revealed that the [spoiler]Warframes are, in fact, merely flesh puppets remotely controlled by [strike]force-sensitive[/strike] teenagers who are the real Tenno. I cannot even begin to explain why I hate this reveal so much. First, it destroys the fun of being this awesome space-ninja-wizard knowing that all you’re doing is tugging on Pinocchio’s strings. Worse, you start to have this teenager butting in every two seconds in each damn mission spouting some throwaway line trying to sound all epic and wise. Then, on top of that, it DESTROYS any potential for tense and interesting storytelling in-universe because it’s pretty much establishes that the Tenno are unstoppable. Even if you kill a ‘Tenno’ all you’ve done is destroyed their warframe. They can easily manufacture another and resume fighting with no problem whatsoever. [/spoiler]This story reveal decreased my interest in the game substantially. I began to view Warframe's story with the same disdain I would a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ YA novel.

With that said, I still like Warframe. Maybe not love, as many seem to. But I do think it’s a pretty great game that at the very least deserves your recognition and consideration. If not for its incredible gameplay, then as a shining example of how to implement Free-to-Play monetization in a sustainable, healthy, and ethical manner.
